Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines portable failure categories for Money behavior.

Requirements

  • MONEY-ERROR-001 — A missing, malformed, non-finite, or unsupported amount MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_AMOUNT and MUST NOT return a Money result.
    Evidence & context1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    Preserve the magnitude of a financial value; do not silently truncate it ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Unsupported amounts fail without a Money result; the interview does not establish a portable supported-range threshold.

    Scope and limitations

    This is a personal recollection, not a verified experiment or a universal statement about COBOL. No details from the withheld follow-up are used. Exact representability does not define universal database field capacity. The Open Questions in spec/money/representation.md leave portable precision, scale and overflow limits unresolved: this behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. Unsupported amounts already have a portable failure category; this comparison does not set the capacity threshold or introduce an overflow code.

  • MONEY-ERROR-002 — A missing or invalid currency identifier MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_CURRENCY and MUST NOT return a Money result.
  • MONEY-ERROR-003 — An operation requiring compatible currencies that receives incompatible currencies MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH and MUST NOT return a Money result.
  • MONEY-ERROR-004 — Division by a zero scalar MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_DIVISION_BY_ZERO and MUST NOT return a Money result.
  • MONEY-ERROR-005 — Required precision reduction without an applicable explicit rounding policy MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_ROUNDING_REQUIRED and MUST NOT return a Money result.
  • MONEY-ERROR-006 — An invalid or unsupported rounding scale or mode MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ROUNDING and MUST NOT return a Money result.
  • MONEY-ERROR-007 — A failed Money operation MUST leave the observable value of every Money operand unchanged.
    Evidence & context1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Legacy / Illustrates a risk

    Treat overlooked exceptions as failure cases worth making observable ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Failed Money operations preserve every operand; negative acceptance artifacts can inspect before/after values.

    Scope and limitations

    The surrounding prediction about the first day of go-live is personal rhetoric, not a measured rate or universal temporal claim. Only failures already defined by the owning specification can acquire expected observations; a test suite must not invent banking exceptions or imply exhaustive correctness.

  • MONEY-ERROR-008 — An allocation request with a missing, malformed, unsupported, invalid, or out-of-range allocation method, part count, ratio list, ratio value, or target scale MUST fail with FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ALLOCATION and MUST NOT return an allocation result.

Implementations can provide additional structured details in accordance with conventions.

Error Codes

CodeMeaning
FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_AMOUNTThe amount is missing, malformed, non-finite, or unsupported.
FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_CURRENCYThe currency identifier is missing or invalid.
FINKORE_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCHAn operation requires compatible currencies but received incompatible ones.
FINKORE_MONEY_DIVISION_BY_ZEROA monetary division used a zero divisor.
FINKORE_MONEY_ROUNDING_REQUIREDPrecision loss would occur without an applicable explicit rounding policy.
FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ROUNDINGThe requested rounding scale or mode is invalid or unsupported.
FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ALLOCATIONThe requested allocation method, count, ratios, or target scale is invalid.

Invariants

A failed operation leaves the observable value of every Money operand unchanged, as required by MONEY-ERROR-007.

For division, MONEY-ARITHMETIC-011 makes the zero-divisor category primary before optional rounding-policy validation. For a non-zero divisor, explicit null, incomplete policy structure, negative or non-integer scale, and an unsupported mode are invalid rounding under MONEY-ERROR-006. These failures return no Money result and leave the operand unchanged.

Non-Goals

This is not a complete catalog and does not define exception, response, or localization formats.
